rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus holds that the interrogative hamza belongs before the conditional answer, yielding the sense “Will you turn back if Muhammad dies?”
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء قال يونس الهمزة في مثل هذا احقها ان تدخل على جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh's placement is preferred: moving the answer before the condition would leave the fāʾ without a role, while the hamza properly takes the front of the whole condition-answer unit.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه الحق لوجهين احدهما انك لو قدمت الجواب لم يكن للفاء وجه

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians rebut Yunus: fronting فهم would leave the condition without an answer, and the preceding clause cannot serve as an omitted answer because the fāʾ attached to إن prevents it; the hamza scopes over the whole construction.
rows.anchor: وقد رد النحويون على يونس

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans take a preceding clause that can answer a later condition as the actual answer, with no ellipsis.
rows.anchor: فلا تقدير عند الكوفيين بل المقدم هو جواب

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans analyze the preceding clause as an indication of an omitted answer to the condition.
rows.anchor: فلا تقدير عند الكوفيين بل المقدم هو جواب وعند البصريين دليل الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the Kufan analysis: a fāʾ would accompany a genuine answer, and fronting the clause changes how the speech is built; Ibn al-Sarrāj and Ibn Mālik also support it.
rows.anchor: والصحيح هو الاول لان الفاء لاتدخل عليه ولو كان جوابا لدخلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object that the construction remains conditional even when the apparent answer comes first, comparing it to an admission of ten less one dirham; the author rejects Ibn al-Sarrāj's claim that it occurs only by necessity because it appears in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ونوزعا في ذلك بل مع التقديم الكلام مبني على الشرط

rows.speaker: ابن السراج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj says this fronting occurs only by poetic necessity; the author rejects that restriction because the Qur’an uses it.
rows.anchor: ثم زعم ابن السراج ان ذلك لا يقع الا في الضرورة وهو مردود بوقوعه في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians would make لن jussive, but most parse it as subjunctive; either way, it negates the future.
rows.anchor: وكان ينبغي إن تكون جازمة وقد قيل به إلا إن الاكثر النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن negates future action more forcefully than لا, as illustrated by “I will not leave the land” compared with “I will not cease until I reach the meeting place.”
rows.anchor: وهي في نفي الاستقبال آكد من لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contrary to the author of al-Anmūdhaj, لن does not mean denial for all eternity: it denies the future unless something later removes that denial; لم is for the past and ما for the present.
rows.anchor: وليس معناها النفي على التأييد خلافا لصاحب الانموذج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن's denial concerns what is near and does not by itself span time as أبدا does; conditional لا with أبدا gives the denial general force across times.
rows.anchor: ومن خواصها انها تنفي ما قرب ولايمتد معنى النفي فيها كامتداد معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reconciles the two claims about wishing for death: conditional لا plus أبدا is general across time, while لن paired with كان in the other verse is limited to the time the condition could obtain.
rows.anchor: فقصر من صيغة النفي لان قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبدا can denote a long period rather than unending duration, as ordinary speech can say someone fasts or prays forever.
rows.anchor: وأما التأبيد فلا يدل على الدوام تقول زيد يصوم ابدا ويصلي ابدا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer from لن that seeing God is impossible; the author says the particle does not establish eternal impossibility.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يبطل تعلق المعتزلة بان لن تدل على امتناع الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes seeing from perceiving: the prophetic report promises that believers will see their Lord but does not say they will perceive Him; Arabs use لن for what is presumed and لا for what is doubtful.
rows.anchor: وأما الإدراك الذي نفي ب لا فلا يمنع من الرؤية

rows.speaker: ابن الخشاب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Khashshāb explicitly says perpetuity means a long span of time, not time that never ends.
rows.anchor: وممن صرح بان التأبيد عبارة عن الزمن الطويل لا عن الذي لا ينقطع ابن الخشاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse about believers who act righteously, وأولئك is the predicate, while إنا لا نضيع أجر من أحسن عملا is a parenthetical clause.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وأولئك ﴾ الخبر وإنا ﴿ لا نضيع ﴾ اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about God loving the purified is an explanatory parenthesis between the command to approach wives after purification and the statement that wives are a field for their husbands.
rows.anchor: ومنها كون الثاني بيانا للأول كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pregnancy and weaning clause interrupts the command to honor parents to remind the child of the mother's hardship, giving her added emphasis because she bore burdens the father did not.
rows.anchor: ومنها تخصيص أحد المذكورين بزيادة التأكيد على أمر علق بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith accordingly gives the mother the recommendation three times and the father once.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث التوصية بالأم ثلاثا وبالأب مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical assurance that God will expose what they concealed shows the Israelites that their dispute over the murdered person cannot hide it; without it, the narrative would proceed directly to the command to strike the corpse.
rows.anchor: وفائدته أن يقرر في أنفس المخاطبين أن تدارؤ بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause God knows best what He sends down interrupts the conditional and its answer as a rejoinder to the accusation that the Prophet fabricated revelation.
rows.anchor: فاعترض بين إذ وجوابها بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One purpose of emphasis is to aggravate the hearer with the emphatic report, illustrated by the affirmation that the Prophet is among the messengers.
rows.anchor: ومنها قصد اغاظة السامع بذلك الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis can encourage: in “He is the Relenting, the Merciful,” إن, the separating pronoun, and emphatic divine attributes strengthen the invitation to repent; “God is with us” is another example.
rows.anchor: ومنها الترغيب كقوله ﴿ فتاب عليكم إنه هو التواب الرحيم ﴾

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators take “guidance from Me” to signal that all good comes from God; the author adds other examples of revelation and proof coming from Him.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون فيه اشارة إلى ان الخير كله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An emphatic statement can allude to a further request: Mary’s “I have given birth to a female” indirectly asks God to accept her offering, since she had sought a boy for the vow.
rows.anchor: ومنها التعريض بأمر آخر كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis should match the hearer's state: an unknowing listener needs none, a doubtful one merits some, and a denier requires stronger emphasis; the messengers answer three denials with three matching forms.
rows.anchor: قالوا انما يؤتى به للحاجة للتحرز عن ذكر مالا فائدة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Our Lord knows” has the force of an oath; it answers the claim that the messengers are liars, alongside “we are messengers” and “our duty is only clear delivery.”
rows.anchor: فقوبلوا على نظيره بثلاثة أشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listeners can be treated as deniers when they are heedless: death receives two emphases, while resurrection receives one because its proofs are clear and should prompt reflection.
rows.anchor: وقد اجتمعا في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning from direct address to third person lets others marvel at the people's conduct and disbelief; continuing to address them would lose that effect.
rows.anchor: وفائدة العدول عن خطابهم إلى حكاية حالهم لغيرهم لتعجبه من فعلهم وكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the opening addresses believers and unbelievers together, so the shift confines blame to the unbelieving group described at the end.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن الخطاب أولا كان مع الناس مؤمنهم وكافرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the passengers felt present and afraid while boarding, but after the favorable wind brought safety they became heedless; the shift then rebukes them as absent.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنهم وقت الركوب حصروا لأنهم خافوا الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage about entering Paradise shifts from address to third person in “they are served,” then shifts back to direct address in “you will remain,” repeating the figure.
rows.anchor: فانتقل عن الخطاب إلى الغيبة ولو ربط بما قبله لقال يطاف عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists charity given for God's sake and God making disbelief and sin hateful as further examples of shifting from address to third person.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وما آتيتم من زكاة تريدون وجه الله فأولئك هم المضعفون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected continuation was “and you divided,” but third person instead reports and reproaches their fragmentation to others, highlighting their offense.
rows.anchor: والأصل فقطعتم عطفا على ما قبله لكن عدل من الخطاب إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajarī counts “nor did He forsake” as a shift to third person; the author rejects this, analyzing it instead as an omitted object.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه ابن الشجري ﴿ ما ودعك ربك وما قلى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إنما, إن supplies confirmation and ما supplies emphatic restriction; the phrase compresses the sense that God is not multiple but is one God.
rows.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى ﴿ إنما الله إله واحد ﴾

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and Thaʿlab, as quoted by al-Ṭarṭūsī, deny that any particle is زائد in the Qur’an; most scholars, jurists, and commentators affirm such particles occur.
rows.anchor: زعم المبرد وثعلب ألا صلة في القرآن والدهماء من العلماء والفقهاء والمفسرين على إثبات الصلات

rows.speaker: ابن السراج
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj says Arabic has no purposeless زائد; examples called زائد should be understood as reinforcement.
rows.anchor: وعند ابن السراج أنه ليس في كلام العرب زائد لأنه تكلم بغير فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects treating زائد as meaningless: the label means the governing word could reach what follows without it, not that it lacks a function; this is the best sense among the views discussed.
rows.anchor: فإنهم إنما سموا ما زائدة هنا لجواز تعدى العامل قبلها إلى ما بعدها

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says no meaningless element occurs in God's speech and construes ما here as an exclamatory interrogative, “by what mercy”; the author rejects his analysis.
rows.anchor: وقد رد على فخر الدين الرازي قوله إن المحققين على أن المهمل لا يقع في كلام الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative reading fails: “what mercy” makes ما construct with رحمة, but only أي can form that exclamatory construction; if ما were a substitute interrogative, a required hamza is absent.
rows.anchor: وأما ما قاله في الآية إنها للاستفهام التعجبي فقد انتقد عليه بأن قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here زائد means an inserted particle serving emphasis, as in “by mercy,” “some example—a gnat,” and “nothing like His likeness.”
rows.anchor: أهل الصناعة يطلقون الزائد على وجوه منها ما يتعلق به هنا وهو ما أقحم تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about ransom elliptically means even if the disbeliever possessed the earth's fill of gold and offered it as ransom, it would not be accepted.
rows.anchor: أي لو ملكا ولو افتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conjunction and its coordinated clause can both be omitted: the sick or traveler who breaks the fast must make up days later.
rows.anchor: ويجوز حذفه مع حرف العطف

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṣfūr and al-Abadhī analyze “the sea parted” as following an omitted “he struck it, and”; deleting the first conjunct also removes its conjunction because no coordinating particle is needed once one conjunct is gone.
rows.anchor: كذا زعم ابن عصفور والأبذي قالوا والذي دل على ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḍāʾiʿ says this is not ellipsis: the consequent stands in place of its cause, and انفلق itself is the answer to the command, as in فانبجست.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الضائع ليس هذا من الحذف بل من إقامة المعطوف مقام المعطوف عليه لأنه سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians disagree about deleting the replaced term and analyze the verse “this is lawful and this is forbidden” as an example.
rows.anchor: حذف المبدل منه اختلفوا فيه وخرج عليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “we believe in what was sent to us and sent to you,” a second relative pronoun is understood before the latter phrase, since what was sent to the first community is not what was sent to earlier communities.
rows.anchor: أي والذي أنزل إليكم لأن الذي أنزل إلينا ليس هو الذي أنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative pronoun من is understood before سارب and before the clause “none of us but has a station”; the text explicitly gives the parallel phrase about one hidden by night and traveling by day.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik restricts omission of a relative pronoun in some writings to cases where it is coordinated with another relative; he says a relative particle is otherwise omitted only if it is أن.
rows.anchor: وشرط ابن مالك في بعض كتبه لجواب الحذف كونه معطوفا على موصول آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the نعم construction, the specifically praised or blamed term may be omitted when context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: حذف المخصوص في باب نعم & إذا علم من سياق الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives the conditional “if the Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship” as an example in the discussion of phrasing an assertion in another form.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative means: should one expect that, if they take charge, they will corrupt the land and sever kinship ties in avid pursuit of worldly life?
rows.anchor: والمعنى هل يتوقع منكم إن توليتم أمور الناس وتأمرتم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presenting the matter as an expectation invites reflection on its consequences and rebukes those whom God has blinded and deafened gently, avoiding direct confrontation and winning their hearts; hence the shift to third person.
rows.anchor: وإنما أورد الكلام في الآية على طريق سوق غير المعلوم سياق غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inevitable or promised event can be cast in the form of possibility, as in the hoped-for praised station, God's bringing victory, mercy, and what people dislike being good for them.
rows.anchor: وقد يخرج الواجب في صورة الممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted can be expressed as conditional: entry into Paradise is barred until a camel passes through a needle's eye.
rows.anchor: وقد يخرج الإطلاق في صورة التقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb means they will never return to the unbelievers' religion: God is known not to will apostasy for prophets, so attaching an action to an impossible condition emphatically negates it.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى لا يكون أبدا من حيث علقه بمشيئة الله

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Quṭrub reads the passage with fronting and delay: the exception belongs to the unbelievers' threat to expel Shuʿayb and his followers unless God wills them to return to their religion.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب في الكلام تقديم وتأخير والاستثناء من الكفار لا من شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Quṭrub's reading, Shuʿayb then declares that his people cannot return to the religion under any circumstance; another view takes the pronoun to refer to the town.
rows.anchor: وقيل الهاء عائدة إلى القرية لا إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about a migrant who dies avoids stating the reward's amount and instead says it rests with God, magnifying an unspecified reward; restating the condition likewise highlights the deed's greatness.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن ذكر مقدار الجزاء والثواب وذكر ما هو معلوم مشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase “We increased them with torment above the torment,” the definite form marks the added torment as different from the torment it is added to.
rows.anchor: تعريفه إن المزيد غير المزيد عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether repeated descriptions denote the same thing or different things cannot be decided categorically; context sometimes indicates difference, as when the criminals call the Day of Judgment an hour unlike their worldly hour or the People of the Book request another book.
rows.anchor: الرابع عكسه فلا يطلق القول به بل يتوقف على القرائن فتارة تقوم قرينة على التغاير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the guidance given to Moses comprises all the religion, miracles, laws, and guidance and direction.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري المراد بالهدى جميع ما آتاه من الدين والمعجزات والشرائع والهدى والارشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In other contexts, repeated descriptions refer to the same thing, as when the Qur’an is described as containing examples and as an Arabic Qur’an, or as both Qur’an and book heard by the jinn.
rows.anchor: وتارة تقوم قرينة على الاتحاد كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated kindness phrase is a case of an indefinite noun recurring as definite; although من معروف comes later in recitation, it preceded بالمعروف in revelation.
rows.anchor: واما قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذن has two uses. The first establishes a causal conditional relation and governs a following future imperfect in the subjunctive when it begins the clause, is uninterrupted, and the verb is not present.
rows.anchor: الأول أن تدل على إنشاء السببية والشرط بحيث لا يفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its second use confirms an answer already linked to a prior statement or marks a cause already present; it does not govern because the link remains clear if إذن is removed, and it can enter a nominal clause.
rows.anchor: والثاني إن تكون مؤكدة لجواب ارتبط بمقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's إذا emphasizes the response and links it to the preceding condition about following others' desires after knowledge.
rows.anchor: فهي مؤكدة للجواب وتربطه بما تقدم

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some later writers propose a third, non-governing use: إذن combines إذ with a following clause, with the clause omitted and its tanwīn serving as substitute, as in حينئذ.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعض المتأخرين لها معنى ثالثا وهي إن تكون مركبة من إذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the proposed third use is not recorded by grammarians: they describe deletion of the clause after إذ, not after إذا; Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn Razīn's account is not a grammatical position.
rows.anchor: واعلم إن هذا المعنى لم يذكره النحاة لكنه قياس قولهم

rows.speaker: القاضي ابن الجويني
rows.claim: Ibn al-Juwaynī thinks إذن أكرمك may take a nominative verb to mean “if you come to me, I will honor you,” with the omitted clause replaced by tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي ابن الجويني وأنا أظن أنه يجوز أن تقول لمن قال أنا آتيك إذن أكرمك بالرفع

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī says he read in al-Junayd's commentary that “neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him” explains the name al-Qayyūm.
rows.anchor: قال البيهقي في شرح الأسماء الحسنى قرأت في تفسير الجنيدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses describing the human as anxious when harmed and withholding when prosperous explain هلوعا; explanatory clauses are common in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا إذا مسه الشر جزوعا وإذا مسه الخير منوعا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For them is forgiveness and a great reward” explains the promise made to believers.
rows.anchor: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God will establish believers in the land is explanatory, not a second object, since the verb وعد takes only one object.
rows.anchor: تفسير للوعد وتبيين له لا مفعول ثان فلم يتعد الفعل منها إلا إلى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God created Jesus from dust explains the likeness between Jesus and Adam.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “they slaughter your sons” and what follows explains the torment Pharaoh's people inflicted.
rows.anchor: وما بعده تفسير للسوم وهو في القرآن كثير

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī says one should not stop before an explanatory clause, because it completes the explanation much like a relative clause or adjective completes its noun.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح بن جنى ومتى كانت الجملة تفسيرا لم يحسن الوقف على ما قبلها دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanatory clause can state the reason for a command: God knows what people conceal and reveal, so their words should not grieve the Prophet; it is not part of the disbelievers' speech.
rows.anchor: وقد يجيء لبيان العلة والسبب كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All might belongs to God” similarly explains why the Prophet should not grieve over what the disbelievers say.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله ﴿ ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians differ on whether an explanatory clause has no syntactic position or takes the position of what it explains when that expression has one; the source also relates this to detailed specification.
rows.anchor: قيل الجملة التفسيرية لا موضع لها من الإعراب وقيل يكون لها موضع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Reports differ on the last revelation in Mecca: Ibn ʿAbbās names al-ʿAnkabūt, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ name al-Muʾminūn, and Mujāhid names “Woe to those who give short measure.” The author says this ordering is established by reliable transmitters and counts 85 Meccan surahs.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا فى آخر ما نزل بمكة فقال ابن عباس العنكبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the preceding analysis of كالوهم and وزنوهم on two grounds: the spelling lacks the alif expected by that reading, and الناس shows that the pronoun refers to the people; thus they take full measure from people but give people short measure.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن تقدم ذكر الناس يدل على أن الضمير راجع إليهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats الشهر as an omitted object, understanding “whoever witnessed the month” as whoever was present in town during it.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري من حذف المفعول قوله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī instead takes الشهر as an adverbial expression, estimating “whoever witnessed the town during the month.”
rows.anchor: وعند أبي على أن الشهر ظرف والتقدير فمن شهد منكم المصر في الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An object may be omitted when a preceding parallel verb supplies it: God erases what He wills and establishes what He wills.
rows.anchor: ومنها تقدم مثله في اللفظ كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples of omitted objects include repelling evil with what is better, changing the earth and the heavens to another form, and the unstated counterpart who spent after the conquest.
rows.anchor: فلما كان المفعول الثاني بلفظ الأول في عمومه واحتياجه إلى الصلة جاز حذفه

rows.speaker: ابن ظفر
rows.claim: Ibn Ẓafar says the object appears in the first command to see because it concerns the chastening at Badr; it is omitted in the later command about the conquest, when the aim was disclosure, assurance, and inviting belief rather than revenge.
rows.anchor: وسبق عن ابن ظفر السر في ذكر المفعول في الأول وحذفه في الثاني في هذه الآية الشريفة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The phrase omits the subject of وعد because the preceding “what our Lord promised us” supplies “your Lord promised you.”
rows.anchor: قوله قبله ﴿ ما وعدنا ربنا ﴾ 1 قال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrestricted wording can encompass everything God promised—judgment, resurrection, reward, punishment, and the other events of the Hereafter—because all of it harms the deniers and even Paradise's bliss is painful to them.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال أطلق ذلك ليتناول كل ما وعد الله من الحساب والبعث والثواب والعقاب
